newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says Russia, Belarus may merge - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says Russia, Belarus may merge - Interfax.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin told Russian media chiefs on Friday that Russia may merge with its small Slav neighbour Belarus in the future, Interfax news agency said.
"Maybe, after all, this will be a single state," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying. The two former Soviet republics have announced plans to seek closer integration but so far Moscow has
Last April Russia and Belarus, where a majority of the population backs closer integration, formed a tighter bilateral community inside the loose 12-member Commonwealth of Independent States.

But Moscow officials have so far made clear that a full merger could only be discussed after Belarus moves further than its current rudimentary stage in economic reforms and improves its record of human rights and political freedoms.
Yeltsin said he would meet Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko on April 2 to discuss further steps in integration between the two states.
"We should seriously advance in our relations and show an example for other Commonwealth states," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying.
